text:
**I’d choose Starling** if you want one app-based UK current account for your salary, bills and everyday spending. There’s no monthly fee, and its **Bills Manager** lets you set rent and bill money aside in a separate “Space” and pay bills directly from it. That makes it easy to see what’s actually left to spend. Starling also charges no fee for debit-card spending or cash withdrawals abroad, and you can pay cash in at a Post Office. ([starlingbank.com](https://www.starlingbank.com/current-account/?utm_source=openai))

**Monzo is the alternative I’d consider** if customer service matters more to you than overseas cash withdrawals. In the August 2026 Great Britain survey, 79% of Monzo customers said they’d recommend it, versus 76% for Starling. Monzo’s standard account is free, but it charges £1 per cash deposit and, outside the European Economic Area, 3% on cash withdrawals above £200 in a rolling 30-day period. ([starlingbank.com](https://www.starlingbank.com/current-account/))

**I’d try Starling before moving your salary.** Use it for everyday spending for a week or two. If you like it, the free Current Account Switch Service moves your balance, Direct Debits and standing orders in seven working days and redirects incoming payments. A full switch **closes your old account**, so wait until you’re ready. ([currentaccountswitch.co.uk](https://www.currentaccountswitch.co.uk/about-the-service/?utm_source=openai))
